forces.title: Strong Demographic Demand Drives Social Care Infrastructure Needs
forces.description: Ireland's social infrastructure sector experiences robust demand from an ageing population and rising chronic disease prevalence. These long-term demographic trends are consistently increasing the need for facilities such as nursing homes, disability accommodation, and community-based care infrastructure, underpinning resilient investment fundamentals and sustained activity in the social care market.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Increased Government Funding Supports Disability and Social Care Services
forces.description: Government funding for disability services in Ireland has seen a significant increase to €3.88bn, with €2.2bn specifically allocated to residential services. This sustained public investment fosters the continued expansion and development of social infrastructure assets, creating a stable and supportive environment for both public and private providers in the residential and community-based care segments.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Capacity Constraints Fuel Investment in Social Care Infrastructure
forces.description: Significant capacity constraints across nursing homes, disability services, and homecare in Ireland are creating compelling opportunities for investment in social infrastructure. The national requirement for an additional 2,197 disability residential places, coupled with ongoing demand for new nursing home development and supported living facilities, acts as a strong driver for capital expenditure in expanding and modernising these essential assets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Workforce Shortages and Rising Costs Pressure Social Infrastructure Margins
forces.description: Despite robust demand, Ireland's healthcare sector, including social infrastructure providers, faces significant operational headwinds from persistent workforce shortages, funding adequacy issues, and increasing payroll and operating costs. These factors constrain provider margins and can impede the ability to invest in and expand essential social infrastructure assets, requiring careful management strategies to maintain financial viability and service quality.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Policy Shift Towards Community-Based Care Reshapes Infrastructure Needs
forces.description: Ireland's healthcare policy is undergoing a structural shift, increasingly prioritising independent living and care closer to home. This trend drives a move towards community-based and home-based care models, projected to increase home care demand by 91% by 2040. This change will fundamentally influence investment priorities for social infrastructure assets, likely favouring distributed, smaller-scale community facilities over traditional large institutional settings.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Ireland's Social Care Infrastructure Offers Resilient Investment Opportunities Amidst Demographic Demand
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland expresses a positive outlook for Ireland's social care infrastructure, citing strong demographic demand from an ageing population and rising chronic diseases. Continued government investment and increasing private sector activity are supporting the expansion of residential and community-based care facilities. The sector benefits from significant investment opportunities in disability accommodation, supported living, respite services, and nursing home development, driven by persistent capacity constraints. Providers with modern infrastructure, strong governance, and capital access are best positioned for long-term growth despite operational cost pressures.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: The population's evolving needs, particularly in disability services, necessitates an expansion of residential and community-based care facilities.
Government policy prioritising independent living and care closer to home increases the need for supportive residential facilities.

new_opportunities.description: The identified national requirement creates significant future investment opportunities for new and expanded disability accommodation assets.
Expansion opportunities exist in supported living and respite services infrastructure to meet the growing national demand.

market_sizing.methodology: The reported figure represents the national requirement for additional residential places in disability services, indicating a clear gap in existing social care infrastructure capacity.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026
